questions.stem: In which Indian state is the famous 'Hornbill Festival' celebrated every year from December 1 to 10?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The Hornbill Festival is a massive cultural extravaganza held every year in the first week of December in Nagaland (at the Naga Heritage Village, Kisama). It is named after the Indian Hornbill, a large and colorful forest bird deeply respected in Naga folklore. The festival brings together all 17 major Naga tribes to showcase their traditional dances, songs, and indigenous games.
DECOY BUSTING: Manipur is famous for the Sangai Festival. Assam celebrates Bihu. Mizoram is famous for the Chapchar Kut festival.
EXAM INSIGHT: Often dubbed the "Festival of Festivals," the state government organizes it to encourage inter-tribal interaction and promote Nagaland's cultural heritage to tourists.

questions.stem: The headquarters of the World Trade Organization (WTO) is located in which city?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The World Trade Organization (WTO) is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland. Established in 1995 (replacing the GATT), it is the only global international organization dealing with the rules of trade between nations.
DECOY BUSTING: New York hosts the UN Headquarters. Paris hosts UNESCO. Vienna hosts OPEC and the IAEA.
EXAM INSIGHT: Geneva is arguably the world capital of international organizations, hosting the headquarters for the WHO (Health), ILO (Labor), WMO (Meteorology), and the Red Cross.

questions.stem: Who was the first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Weightlifter Karnam Malleswari made history at the 2000 Sydney Olympics by winning the bronze medal in the 69kg category, becoming the very first Indian woman to ever stand on an Olympic podium.
DECOY BUSTING: P.T. Usha (the 'Payyoli Express') famously missed a bronze medal by 1/100th of a second in 1984. Mary Kom won bronze in boxing in 2012. Saina Nehwal won bronze in badminton in 2012.
EXAM INSIGHT: The first Indian to win an individual Olympic medal (post-independence) was K.D. Jadhav (Wrestling bronze, 1952 Helsinki).
